body:
web/src/i18n/__android__/de.json is a 72-key subset of the Android German
catalog, and consistency.test.ts asserts web German matches it. Nothing
verifies the snapshot still matches the real
android/app/src/main/res/values-de/strings.xml, so it drifts silently.

It had drifted: it still carried item.addAnother long after the Android string
was deleted, which is part of why [[T-144]]'s divergence went unnoticed. Fixed
by hand in the T-144 commit, which is the same manual step that let it drift in
the first place.

The comment in consistency.test.ts says the cross-client half of the check
"lives in the Android suite, where the resource XML is readable without a build
step". It does not. TranslationResourcesTest only compares Android locales
against Android English. So the claim is wrong and there is no automated
cross-client check at all.

Two ways out:
1. Have the web test read values-de/strings.xml directly (it is a fixed relative
   path from web/, and the test already normalises the two placeholder dialects)
   and drop the snapshot.
2. Generate the snapshot from the resources as a build step, so drift is a diff.

Option 1 removes a file rather than adding a generator, and makes a deleted
Android string fail the web suite immediately.
title: cross-client i18n check is a hand-kept snapshot nothing validates
